status: candidate: tasks written by OpenPath (AI-prepared); done with a grown-up, who ticks what they saw; not reviewed by an educator
evidence: practice-only: the app does not hear or mark these; an adult's ticks are kept as a record and change no capability estimate

tasks.title: My favourite game
tasks.task: Tell a grown-up about your favourite game for one minute. Say what it is, how it is played and why you like it.
look: Gave a reason for liking it

tasks.title: A rule I would change
tasks.task: Choose one rule at home or at school that you would change. Explain your idea and why it would be better.

tasks.title: Ask three questions
tasks.task: Ask a grown-up three questions about their school days. Listen to each answer before you ask the next question.
look: Asked one question that followed from an answer

tasks.title: Answer in full sentences
tasks.task: Ask a grown-up to ask you three questions about your day. Answer each one in a full sentence.
look: Added a detail without being asked

tasks.title: Find out and tell
tasks.task: With a grown-up, look up one animal in a book or on the internet. Then tell them three things you learnt, in your own words.
look: Used own words, not read aloud

tasks.title: Two places to look
tasks.task: Pick a question, such as why the sky is blue. Find the answer in two places and say whether they agree.

tasks.title: Guess the feeling
tasks.task: Ask a grown-up to say "Come here" in three ways: happy, cross and worried. Say which is which, and how you could tell.
look: Pointed to the voice or the face as the clue

tasks.title: Words and face
tasks.task: Ask a grown-up to say "I am fine" while looking tired. Say what the words tell you and what the face tells you.
look: Noticed the words and the face differ
Said which to believe and why

tasks.title: The same and different
tasks.task: Listen while a grown-up tells you about a festival or a holiday from their childhood. Tell them one thing that is the same for you and one that is different.
look: Gave one thing that is the same
Gave one thing that is different

tasks.title: It reminds me of
tasks.task: After reading a story in the app, tell a grown-up what it reminds you of in your own life.
look: Made a link to own life

tasks.title: Stand and speak
tasks.task: Stand up and tell a grown-up how to make a cup of tea, step by step. Look at them while you speak.
look: Spoke at a steady pace, not too fast
Used hands to help show a step

tasks.title: Read it aloud
tasks.task: Read a short text from the app aloud to a grown-up. Stop at each full stop and look up once in every sentence.

tasks.title: A small project
tasks.task: With a grown-up, choose a topic such as rivers. Use a computer, a phone or a library to find five facts and write them in a list.
look: Wrote the facts in own words

tasks.title: Where did it come from?
tasks.task: For a fact you found, say where you found it and why you trust that place.
look: Named the place it came from
Gave a reason to trust it
Said what to do if two places disagree

tasks.title: A book of my choice
tasks.task: Read a story book or a part of one that is not in this app. Tell a grown-up who is in it and what happens.

tasks.title: What I thought of it
tasks.task: After reading a book or a poem, tell a grown-up one thing you liked and one thing you would change.

tasks.title: A poem aloud
tasks.task: Choose a short poem from a book at home or at school. Read it aloud to a grown-up and say what picture it puts in your mind.
look: Named a word or line that made the picture

tasks.title: Yes or no?
tasks.task: A grown-up says: "Children should have homework every day." Say whether you agree, and give two reasons.

tasks.title: Talk about the weather
tasks.task: Talk with a grown-up about the weather this week. Take turns: say something, then listen, then answer what they said.
look: Answered what the other person said

tasks.title: Plan a picnic together
tasks.task: Plan a picnic with a grown-up. Decide together where to go, what to carry and what to eat.

tasks.title: Answer and add
tasks.task: Ask a grown-up to ask you: "What did you do at school today?" Answer, then add one more thing they did not ask about.

tasks.title: What do you think?
tasks.task: A grown-up tells you about a film or a book they like. Say one thing you think about it and ask one question.
look: Made a comment on the topic

tasks.title: Tell me about an animal
tasks.task: Choose an animal. Tell a grown-up about it in order: what it looks like, where it lives and what it eats.

tasks.title: What the text said
tasks.task: Read a text in the app. Then tell a grown-up what it said, from the beginning to the end.

tasks.title: A day I remember
tasks.task: Tell a grown-up about a day you remember well. Say what happened first, next and last.

tasks.title: Tell a story you know
tasks.task: Tell a grown-up a story you know well, such as a folk tale, without reading it.
look: Had a beginning, a middle and an end

tasks.title: A tongue twister
tasks.task: Ask a grown-up to teach you a tongue twister. Say it slowly, then try it three times fast.

tasks.title: A riddle each
tasks.task: Ask a grown-up to tell you a riddle, and try to answer it. Then tell them a riddle or a short poem you know.
look: Had a go at the answer
Shared a riddle or a poem

tasks.title: It happened to me too
tasks.task: After reading a story in the app, tell a grown-up about a time something like it happened to you.
look: Said how the two are alike

tasks.title: What would I do?
tasks.task: After reading a story in the app, tell a grown-up what you would have done in the place of the main person.

tasks.title: A book of my choice
tasks.task: Read a story book or a part of one that is not in this app. Tell a grown-up what it is about.

tasks.title: Read for ten minutes
tasks.task: Read anything you like for ten minutes: a comic, a magazine or a book. Tell a grown-up one thing you enjoyed.

tasks.title: Look it up
tasks.task: Choose a word you do not know. With a grown-up, find it in a dictionary, on paper or on a phone, and read out what it means.
look: Used the word in a sentence

tasks.title: Another word for it
tasks.task: Choose a word such as big or happy. With a grown-up, find two other words that mean nearly the same.
look: Said how they differ a little

tasks.title: Lead the talk
tasks.task: Lead a short family discussion on a question, such as whether pets belong in flats. Ask each person a question and sum up at the end.

tasks.title: Dig deeper
tasks.task: A grown-up gives an opinion. Ask three questions that make them explain it further, such as "Why do you think so?"

tasks.title: Make your case
tasks.task: Say whether school uniforms are a good idea. Use at least three exact words such as fair, practical or expensive.

tasks.title: Persuade me
tasks.task: Persuade a grown-up to try a food, a game or a book that you like.
look: Used persuading words such as because or imagine

tasks.title: Present what you found
tasks.task: Give a two-minute talk on a topic you have read about. Say where each main fact came from.
look: Kept facts apart from own views

tasks.title: Two views
tasks.task: Present a topic on which people disagree, such as zoos. Give one view, then the other, and say whose view each is.

tasks.title: Stay calm
tasks.task: Give your opinion on a topic while a grown-up disagrees with you. Keep your voice steady and answer politely.

tasks.title: Question an opinion
tasks.task: A grown-up gives an opinion. Question it politely: ask for a reason and for an example.

tasks.title: Answer the other side
tasks.task: A grown-up argues the opposite of what you think. Answer each of their points in turn, with a reason.
look: Used phrases such as I see your point, but

tasks.title: Change one mind
tasks.task: Take a topic you both disagree on. Find the strongest point on the other side and say why it does not change your view.
look: Named the other side's best point
Used hands and face to help the meaning

tasks.title: Read an advertisement
tasks.task: Look at an advertisement in a newspaper or on a hoarding. Tell a grown-up which words are meant to make you want the thing.

tasks.title: Headline and story
tasks.task: Read a newspaper headline and the report under it. Say whether the headline is fair to the report.

tasks.title: Two ways to say it
tasks.task: Ask to borrow a pen twice: once as you would ask a friend, once as you would ask the head teacher.
look: Changed the words for each listener

tasks.title: On the telephone
tasks.task: Pretend to telephone a shop to ask whether it has a book. A grown-up plays the shopkeeper.
look: Greeted and said who was calling

tasks.title: Inform, then persuade
tasks.task: Tell a grown-up the facts about cycling to school. Then try to persuade them that everyone should do it.
look: Kept the first part to facts
Used persuading language in the second

tasks.title: Just my opinion
tasks.task: Give your opinion of a film or a match. Use phrases that show it is an opinion, such as I think and in my view.
look: Did not present opinion as fact

tasks.title: Talk with pictures
tasks.task: Give a short talk about a place, using three pictures or drawings. Show each one as you speak about it.
look: Showed each at the right moment
Spoke about the picture, not just held it up

tasks.title: A chart to explain
tasks.task: Draw a simple chart or map and use it to explain something, such as your way to school.
look: Made a clear chart or map

tasks.title: The same news twice
tasks.task: Find one piece of news in two places, such as a newspaper and the radio. Say what each told you and why it matters.

tasks.title: Read a chart
tasks.task: Find a chart or table in a newspaper or a book. Tell a grown-up what it shows and one thing you can conclude from it.

tasks.title: A book of my choice
tasks.task: Read a book or a long story that is not in this app. Tell a grown-up about the people in it and how it ends.
look: Named the book and its kind

tasks.title: A different kind of text
tasks.task: Read something that is not a story: a life story, a travel piece or a report. Tell a grown-up how it differs from a story.
look: Said how it differs from a story

tasks.title: Two sources, one note
tasks.task: Choose a topic. Read about it in a book and on a website, and write five notes that bring both together.
look: Used a printed and a digital source

tasks.title: Where it came from
tasks.task: For three facts you have gathered, write down where each one came from.
look: Listed a source for each fact
Wrote the title or the site name
Said which source seems most reliable

tasks.title: How do you say it?

tasks.title: One word, many meanings

tasks.title: My morning

tasks.title: A story I know

tasks.title: Describe a thing

look: Gave its colour, size or shape

tasks.title: My favourite place

Gave a sound or a smell

tasks.title: Show and tell

tasks.title: Act a story
